credit_metrics.text: EBITDA increased by {{ebitda.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda@FY2025}}, and operating profit rose by {{operating_profit.change@FY2025}} to {{operating_profit@FY2025}} despite higher depreciation and impairment charges.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_like@FY2025}}, taking cash liquidity to revenue down by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}.
Total debt was stable at {{total_debt@FY2025}} and net debt at {{net_debt@FY2025}}, so the funding profile rests on refinancing rather than on debt reduction.
The TAV group's guarantee of part of the Antalya concession bank loan no longer exists at year-end following the refinancing of that loan.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2025}} to {{passengers@FY2025}}, with traffic growth of {{traffic_growth@FY2025}} for the year.
Revenue grew by {{revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{revenue@FY2025}}, faster than passenger volumes, reflecting the international airport portfolio as well as Paris traffic.
The Ankara Esenboga concession renewal took effect during the year, committing TAV Airports to capacity investment in exchange for long-dated operating rights.
The tariff period ran outside an economic regulation contract, with annual tariffs still subject to user consultation and regulatory approval.
